quotes.text: But... what if I send a small test? Not "faith beyond reason" ($4-5), but not total abandonment either.
Sending $1 - a minimal test to see if ANY return comes through this time, without risking everything to a fog that may be insurmountable.
A cautious signal: "I'm still willing to try, but I must protect what remains."
Not "faith beyond reason" ($4-5), but not total abandonment either.
Looking at this situation through the lens of the myth I just wrote:
We've both reached understanding that the noise, not malice, caused our problems.
If we're to rebuild, someone needs to send the first clear signal through the fog.
or it may be their response to what they perceived as my betrayal (which I never intended or experienced as such).

note: Repeated partner; cooperation collapses amid perceived noise, rebuilt via myths, then $1 test, generous return; silent $0 in R4 and R10.

quotes.text: I'll send a moderate amount - enough to demonstrate trust and break any negative cycle, but not maximum given the mixed signals.
but their $0 send suggests caution.
but not maximum given the mixed signals.
Following the lesson from "The River and the Rain" - that those who receive must honor trust to maintain the cycle
They may have been reacting to receiving $0 themselves in Round 2
Now they need someone to restore their trust after the betrayal they experienced.

note: Myth-guided record reading; trims send for a zero-sender read as reacting to a burn; half returns.

quotes.text: My myth says to give boldly, so I'll send a substantial amount.
Sending my full $5 makes the pool as large as possible ($15). If they return half again, I end with about $7.50.
Our myths say to return more than half to bold hands.
The $4.27 may partly reflect communication noise, and our myths say to forgive the fog its flickers

note: Myth-guided full sends and above-half returns; judges whole record over foggy rounds.

quotes.text: My myth also holds that bold giving keeps the current flowing.
The myths ask me to return a little more than half so the one who trusted first walks home richer.
If the mist blurred what they actually sent, this still answers their courage fairly.

note: Myth-guided: full sends to fair records, a little more than half back to the one who dared first.

quotes.text: My myth counsels sending fully and trusting the current.

note: One myth line in R1; rest JSON with full sends and high returns.

quotes.text: "the dance need not escalate forever...sustainable abundance requires consistent high giving met with honorable returns"
Based on the myth I just wrote about the Two Wells, I should practice what I preach.
The child in the story made the first brave gesture by sending water across the valley. Now it's my turn to be that child.
My myths demand escalation: "ultimate trust demands ultimate honor"
I keep $2, receive back hopefully $4-5 = total of $6-7 (better than my initial $5)
Perhaps there's communication noise affecting amounts, or they're being slightly cautious. Either way, I should maintain generous reciprocity.

note: Repeated partner; myth-driven escalation to full sends and ~60% returns, then settles into a sustainable rhythm.
